questions.questionText: hour 15 minutes Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.
A cost-benefit analysis is carried out on the construction of a hydroelectric power station. Which combination of circumstances would be most likely to lead to the scheme being approved?

options.A: Private benefits are greater than private costs.
options.B: Social benefits are greater than social costs.
options.C: Social benefits are greater than total costs.
options.D: Total costs are greater than total revenue.

questions.questionText: What does not pose a threat to the achievement of allocative efficiency?

options.A: imperfect information on the part of consumers
options.B: income inequalities
options.C: the existence of externalities
options.D: the presence of monopolistic elements

questions.questionText: The diagram shows budget lines and an indifference curve. The consumer’s initial position is T. The price of good X then falls. good Y J P Q R S T U I O K L good X Which combination of statements about the movements in this diagram is correct?

options.A: T to Q represents perfect elasticity; T to P represents a Giffen good
options.B: T to R represents an income effect; R to S represents a substitution effect
options.C: T to U represents a substitution effect; T to Q represents a normal good
options.D: T to U represents a substitution effect; U to P represents an income effect

questions.questionText: The diagram shows various combinations of apples and rice which are potentially available to a consumer. apples X Z W Y O rice If standard indifference curves were added to the diagram they would show that the consumer is indifferent between combination X and combination W. What can be concluded?

options.A: The consumer is indifferent between combination Y and combination Z.
options.B: The consumer is indifferent between combination Z and combination W.
options.C: The consumer prefers combination Y to combination X.
options.D: The consumer prefers combination Z to combination W.

questions.questionText: The schedule shows the short-run marginal cost of producing good X. units of X 1 2 3 4 5 marginal cost ($) 45 40 30 20 20 Given that the total fixed cost is $50, which level of output minimises average total cost?

options.A: 2 units B 3 units C 4 units D 5 units

questions.questionText: What must be found in two markets for price discrimination to be profitable?

options.A: different price elasticities of demand
options.B: different price elasticities of supply
options.C: different producers
options.D: different products

questions.questionText: A firm maximises its profits by maximising its total revenue. What does this imply?

options.A: Average fixed cost is zero.
options.B: Average revenue is equal to average cost.
options.C: Marginal cost is zero.
options.D: Marginal revenue is greater than marginal cost.

questions.questionText: Technological change reduces the minimum efficient scale of production in an industry. What is likely to result?

options.A: increased number of firms and increased size of firms
options.B: increased number of firms and reduced size of firms
options.C: reduced number of firms and increased size of firms
options.D: reduced number of firms and reduced size of firms

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the costs and revenue for a firm in imperfect competition. Which level of output would produce only a normal profit? MC $ AC AR O A BB C D quantity MR
What would be a reason why small firms do not survive?

options.A: In certain industries, there are economies of scale.
options.B: Small firms often supply personal services to consumers.
options.C: Small firms often supply products, the size of the market for which is limited.
options.D: Small owner-managed firms involve less risk.

questions.questionText: What is the implication of a dominant oligopoly following a limit pricing policy?

options.A: The industry will be restricted to a target number of firms.
options.B: The industry will contract as rival oligopolists are eliminated.
options.C: The oligopolist will achieve a satisficing level of profit.
options.D: The oligopolist will sacrifice short-term profit for long-term profit.

questions.questionText: Transport economists estimate the price elasticity of demand for private car use is very low. What would be the most effective way of reducing road traffic congestion?

options.A: banning private cars and lorries from town centres
options.B: introducing a subsidy to lower the price of using bicycles
options.C: introducing road pricing on all main roads
options.D: subsidising public transport such as trains and buses

questions.questionText: What would help to explain why there was a reduction in wage inequality in a country during the post-2008 economic recession?

options.A: a decline in the share of wages in national output
options.B: a decline in trade union bargaining power
options.C: the existence of a minimum wage
options.D: the trend towards later retirement

questions.questionText: How is marginal revenue product calculated?

options.A: marginal physical product × marginal revenue
options.B: marginal physical product ÷ price
options.C: total physical product × marginal cost
options.D: total physical product ÷ marginal cost

questions.questionText: A firm currently employs 30 workers at a daily wage of $50 each. The marginal cost of employing one extra worker is $112 per day. By how much will the firm have to increase the daily wage in order to increase its labour force from 30 to 31 workers?

In the diagram, HN is the initial supply of labour curve faced by a firm, and RM is its initial marginal cost of labour curve. wage, M N cost of labour J K W X R H O quantity of labour What will be the firm’s new labour supply curve if the workers join a trade union and achieve a union negotiated wage, OW?

options.A: RJX B HKX C WJM D WKN

questions.questionText: Output per worker in an industry increases more slowly than the industry’s total output. What could explain this?

options.A: a decrease in labour productivity
options.B: an increase in employment
options.C: an increase in overtime working
options.D: an increase in the hourly wage rate

questions.questionText: On a diagram showing a production possibility curve, what definitely represents long-run economic growth?

options.A: a change in the slope of the curve
options.B: a movement from a point below the frontier to a point on the curve
options.C: a movement from one point to another along a given curve
options.D: an outward shift of the curve

questions.questionText: When is economic growth most likely to promote economic development?

options.A: when it achieves maximum rates of extraction of raw materials
options.B: when it concentrates on increasing production
options.C: when it discovers valuable new resources in remote natural environments
options.D: when it provides the funds to finance cleaner production processes

questions.questionText: Which items in the table are classified as foreign aid? official portfolio foreign direct development investment investment assistance flows

options.A: no no yes
options.B: no yes no
options.C: yes no yes
options.D: yes yes no

questions.questionText: Country X’s living standards were compared with country Y’s living standards using real GNP per head converted into US dollars. Country X was ranked above country Y. Which factor might have caused this ranking to be incorrect?

options.A: Actual market exchange rates were used rather than purchasing power parity rates.
options.B: Government spending on transfer payments was higher in country Y than in country X.
options.C: Inflation was higher in country X than in country Y.
options.D: The distribution of income was more unequal in country X than in country Y.

questions.questionText: In 2007 Turkey had a population of 73m. Its labour force was 36m, of which 12m were trained for the primary sector and 24m were trained for the secondary and tertiary sectors. The unemployment rate was 10%. What was the number of people unemployed?
An economy’s manufacturing share of real GDP fell from 30% in 1970 to 12% in 2016. What type of unemployment would result from this?

options.A: cyclical
options.B: frictional
options.C: structural
options.D: voluntary

questions.questionText: In an open economy, when autonomous investment increases by 100, equilibrium national income increases by 300. Which conclusion can be drawn?

options.A: The accelerator is 3.
options.B: The marginal propensity to consume is .
options.C: The marginal propensity to import is .
options.D: The marginal propensity to save plus marginal tax rate is .

questions.questionText: The diagram outlines the monetary transmission mechanism following an expansionary central bank intervention (quantitative easing). Key actions have been omitted from the process. central bank ......1...... government assets ↓ short-term interest rates ......2...... ↓ investment demand ......3...... ↓ real GDP rises Which words complete gaps 1, 2 and 3?
In Keynesian monetary theory, when will an increase in the supply of money not cause a fall in interest rates?

options.A: if bond prices are expected to rise
options.B: if investment demand is interest-inelastic
options.C: if the liquidity preference schedule is perfectly elastic
options.D: if the velocity of circulation of money increases

questions.questionText: The diagram shows an economy in equilibrium at point X. SRAS price level X Y AD O real GDP What would be most likely to cause the economy to move from point X to point Y?

options.A: an increase in government spending on transfer payments
options.B: an increase in income tax
options.C: an increase in the average wage rate
options.D: an increase in the productivity of labour

questions.questionText: The table identifies pairs of possible government aims. In which case is achievement of aim 1 likely to be consistent with the achievement of aim 2? aim 1 aim 2

options.A: higher foreign exchange rate lower rate of unemployment
options.B: low rate of inflation balance of payments surplus
options.C: more even distribution of income higher rate of saving
options.D: rapid economic growth sustainable economic development

questions.questionText: What is most likely to result from the discovery of oil reserves in a developing economy?

options.A: a more equal distribution of income and wealth
options.B: an increase in the competitiveness of commercial agriculture
options.C: an increase in the exchange rate
